messages:
maria_ps: Hey team — customer ACME reported a billing/usage mismatch. Their client-side SDK estimator reports ~12,120 tokens for request id 0xabc123, but the server invoice and X-Token-Count header show 8,345. Is this a known thing? :thinking:

alex_k: Which SDK version and exact payload? Often small differences in system messages or tool args cause deltas.

maria_ps: SDK: redwood-js@0.9.2. Repro (sanitized):
```js
await client.chat.create({
  model: 'rw-infer-3b',
  messages: [
    { role: 'system', content: 'You are a helpful assistant.' },
    { role: 'user', content: 'Long prompt with ~9k tokens...' },
    { role: 'tool', name: 'lookup', content: JSON.stringify({ id: 42, nested: '...large blob...' }) }
  ],
  tools: [{ name: 'lookup', url: 'https://acme.tools/lookup' }]
})
```
Estimator output (SDK): 12120 tokens

samir: Can you POST the exact same payload to the API (curl) and share response headers? Server exposes X-Token-Count in headers.

maria_ps: Did that. curl -> /v1/chat, same body. Response headers: `X-Token-Count: 8345`. Logs attached.
```
> curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d @payload.json -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< X-Token-Count: 8345
< X-Request-ID: 0xabc123
```

alex_k: Interesting. Two possibilities off the top:
- SDK estimator is counting the tool content twice (once in the prompt, once in a synthetic tool-arg concat)
- Tokenizer/version mismatch between SDK (embedded tokenizer) and server (updated tokenizer pipeline)

samir: Also check normalization (NFC vs NFD) and invisible whitespace — the SDK's tokenizer implementation we ship doesn't normalize Unicode the same way server-side in v0.11 of the token service. That can shift counts by a few %, but this is larger.

maria_ps: I tried removing the tool message (kept system + user). SDK estimate -> 8402 tokens, server header -> 8389. With tool calls present SDK jumps to 12120 but server stays ~8345. So reproduces locally: tool payload appears double-counted by SDK estimator.

alex_k: Good repro. Please include a minimal gist with the exact JSON and the SDK estimator output. Tag eng-ml and devex. We need: request id, model name, tokenizer version in SDK (npm ls redwood-tokenizer), and whether the tool response is streamed or buffered.

billing-bot: Invoice INV-2025-07 includes that usage. Placing a temporary credit hold for the disputed items and opening a billing dispute ticket: https://console.redwood.ai/billing/invoices/INV-2025-07 :white_check_mark:

samir: Action items:
- maria_ps: upload gist + attach stdout of `npm ls redwood-tokenizer` and the SDK estimate log.
- alex_k: create a devex bug and assign to 'tokenizer' owner.
- billing-bot: maintain hold until engineering confirms.

maria_ps: Gist posted: https://gist.github.com/maria_ps/abcd1234 (includes payload, curl, SDK logs). Request IDs: 0xabc123 (customer), 0xabc123-local (repro). Thanks all, keeping this thread updated. :v:
